overview: Santasiere's Folly is a Reti-like set-up with b4 and Bb2, usually reached by 1.Nf3 d5 2.b4 Nf6 3.Bb2 e6 4.e3. White gains queenside space and puts the bishop on the long diagonal; Black can challenge with ...a5 or ...c5 or grab on b4. It is offbeat system play for White rather than main-line theory.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto Bb2, support b4 with a3 and c4
Aim at the long diagonal and play for queenside space
Develop with e3, Be2 and castle short

typical_structures.structure: White flank pawns on b4 and a3, symmetrical-ish centre with Black pawn on d5

character.notes: Quiet manoeuvring with no early forcing lines.

gambit.notes: b4 is not simply hanging, so not really a gambit.

soundness.notes: Playable though slightly worse than main lines.

approach.notes: Rare, played by few strong players.

character.reason: Quiet flank set-up, neither especially safe nor forcing.

gambit.reason: Normal development, b4 is not hanging by force.

structure.reason: Centre not yet resolved, flank opening.

level.reason: Plans are clear but the structure takes judgement.

plans.reason: Bb2 and the b4 push define the set-up.
